body: Boaz R. Weinstein, through Saba Capital Management, disclosed a 5.87% stake in Blackstone Long-Short Credit Income Fund. The Schedule 13D was filed on Oct. 21, 2026 after open-market purchases totaling about $7.9 million. Saba says the fund looks undervalued and plans to press on the share price discount and structure.Investor IntentSaba plans active engagement with management and the board on strategy, governance, and the fund’s structure. The firm may “nominate one or more individuals as nominees for election to the Board” and could “solicit proxies” to support its agenda.The group aims to address the fund’s discount to net asset value and is prepared to push for “share buy-backs, tenders, and liquidations,” and even a change to the investment manager. Saba may also seek changes tied to the fund’s open- or closed-end status and the timing of any potential liquidation.Investor's BackgroundSaba Capital Management, L.P. is a Delaware limited partnership that manages private and public funds, with Boaz R. Weinstein as its founder and chief investment decision-maker. The firm is known for credit-focused and closed-end fund strategies, often using activism to narrow discounts to net asset value. Weinstein, a U.S. investor, gained prominence for high-conviction credit trades and event-driven campaigns.Original SEC Filing: Blackstone Long-Short Credit Income Fund [ BGX ] - SCHEDULE 13D - Oct. 21, 2026DisclaimerThis is an AI-powered summary.
